summary: The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are run by the Swiss federal scholarship commission for foreign students (FCS, also called ESKAS) with the State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation. They support international exchange and research cooperation with applicants from 183 countries. For 2027-2028 there are research fellowships (6 to 12 months), PhD scholarships (12 months, renewable to 36) and art scholarships for a first Master in Arts, all in Switzerland. Holders receive CHF 2,450 per month plus several smaller benefits; tuition is not covered.
eligibility_notes:
Research fellowships: for early-career researchers who are doing a PhD outside Switzerland, including young medical doctors, in any discipline. Applicants who have never studied or researched in Switzerland get priority. You need a Master's degree or equivalent completed by 31 July 2027 (30 June 2027 for ETH Zurich), and you must have been born after 31 December 1991. You need a detailed research plan with timeline and milestones and a support letter from an academic supervisor at a Swiss institution. If you already live in Switzerland, your entry date must be 1 August 2026 or later.

PhD scholarships: same rules as research fellowships, for researchers with a Master's degree in any field who want to do a PhD at a Swiss university or recognised research institute. Applicants new to Switzerland get priority. If you apply through a doctoral school, you must send the school's admission confirmation with the application and also the supervisor's support letter. If the school does not allow contact with a supervisor before admission, you cannot apply. Applicants in a formal cotutelle (joint doctorate with a foreign university) can only receive the 12-month research fellowship, with two supervisors. The scholarship application and the doctoral admission application are separate procedures.

Art scholarships (Master in Arts): for young artists with a Bachelor's degree or equivalent completed by 31 July 2027, born after 31 December 1991, with no Master's degree at the start of the scholarship. You need an admission letter, or proof of application (conditional admission is accepted), from a Swiss university of the arts or music. Art scholarships are offered only to applicants from a limited number of countries. Applicants new to Switzerland get priority, and the same entry-date rule applies (1 August 2026 or later if already in Switzerland).

The overview page also states a maximum age of 35. Eligible countries and scholarship types differ per country and are listed in the official A-Z list; some countries have no scholarship offer.

Exclusion criteria for research and PhD applications: an incomplete or formally flawed application; several applications at the same time to different hosts or scholarship types; living, studying or working in Switzerland for more than 13 months before the scholarship starts; having held a Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship before; a fourth application after three unsuccessful ones (the FAQ allows at most three applications for the same type); no named Swiss supervisor or no supervisor letter; more than one research proposal; and doctoral-school applicants without admission confirmation.

The FAQ says the Swiss government offers no alternative funding if you do not meet the criteria. Postdoctoral scholarships are no longer awarded from the 2027/28 academic year.
age_experience_notes: Born after 31 December 1991 for all three types; the overview page also states a maximum age of 35. Research and PhD applicants need a completed Master's degree or equivalent; art applicants need a Bachelor's degree and no Master's. No years of work experience are stated.
funding_summary: The grant is CHF 2,450 per month for one person's basic living costs; it is a grant, not a salary. Research fellowships last 6 to 12 months with no extension. PhD scholarships run 12 months and can be renewed twice, up to 36 months in total, depending on academic progress. Art scholarships run 12 months and can be extended to at most 21 months depending on the Master's programme and its ECTS credits. All start on 1 September 2027. Further benefits are a rental deposit grant, health insurance premiums and a flight allowance for non-EU/EFTA holders, and a half-fare public transport card. Tuition and semester fees are not covered.
programmes_note: Research fellowships and PhD scholarships are open to any discipline; the PhD or research project must be at a Swiss higher education institution or recognised research institute and carried out full-time in Switzerland. Art scholarships are for a first Master's in an artistic field (music, visual arts, and other artistic domains such as dance, acting or writing) at a Swiss art school or conservatory, and are open only to some countries. The official page does not list individual Master or PhD programme names.
institutions_note: Research and PhD: University of Basel, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva, Lausanne, Lucerne, Neuchatel, St. Gallen, Zurich, Universita della Svizzera italiana, EPFL, ETH Zurich, the ETH Domain research institutes (PSI, WSL, Empa, Eawag), the Graduate Institute (IHEID), universities of applied sciences (HES-SO, BFH, FHNW, OST, FHGR, HSLU, SUPSI, ZHAW), universities of teacher education, UniDistance Suisse (presence in Switzerland required), SFUVET and SFISM Magglingen. Art: HES-SO, Bern University of the Arts (HKB-BFH), FHNW, OST, HSLU, SUPSI, Conservatorio della Svizzera italiana and Zurich University of the Arts (ZHdK). You must find a Swiss supervisor yourself; neither the scholarship secretariat nor the universities help with this, and the search can take weeks or months. Suitable supervisors are professors and laboratory group leaders; for a PhD the supervisor must be authorised to supervise doctoral theses. At universities of applied sciences a doctorate needs two supervisors, one authorised to confer doctorates at a traditional university.

summary.detail: Art scholarship (Master in Arts): funds a first Master's degree at a Swiss art school or conservatory, full-time in Switzerland. 12 months, extendable to a maximum of 21 months depending on the programme and required ECTS credits. For applicants with a Bachelor's degree or equivalent and no Master's, from a limited number of countries. Selection looks at artistic profile, qualifications and motivation, a portfolio showing artistic maturity and potential, and enrolment availability at the chosen university.

PhD scholarships: 12 months, renewable twice up to 36 months in total subject to progress, any field, for holders of a Master's degree or equivalent. Research fellowships: one-year (6 to 12 months) research project as part of a doctorate, no extension. Both are full-time in Switzerland and need a Swiss academic supervisor's support letter.

benefits.limit_text: CHF 2,450 per month for one person's basic living expenses
benefits.conditions: A grant, not a salary. No family allowances. Additional income (other scholarships, assistant positions) must be reported, and the scholarship may not supplement full-time employment.
Rent itself is not covered; it comes out of the monthly grant.

benefits.limit_text: Premiums for compulsory health insurance paid by the commission
benefits.conditions: Only for holders from outside the EU/EFTA. EU/EFTA holders pay their own.

benefits.limit_text: Return flight allowance for non-EU/EFTA holders, based on country of origin; Half-Fare Travelcard for public transport
benefits.conditions: The flight allowance must be used within two months after the scholarship ends and only for the return trip. Travel costs for EU/EFTA holders are not covered.

benefits.limit_text: Excursions and activities organised by the coordinating body
Tuition and semester fees are paid by the holder; some institutions charge about CHF 600 to 2,000 per semester or a reduced fee
benefits.conditions: Some PhD fees are not waived.
PhD holders may ask for up to six months of fieldwork without extra funding. No fieldwork outside Switzerland during research fellowships.
Residence permits for accompanying family are decided by federal and cantonal authorities, which currently apply a restrictive policy; the commission and institutions offer no support.

requirements.text: Complete CV: education, degrees, awards, positions, publications, teaching and practical experience (art applicants: exhibitions or concerts instead of publications).
Research proposal on the FCS/ESKAS form, maximum 5 pages including a non-specialist summary, with a detailed timeline. Only one research proposal may be submitted.

Letter of support from a Swiss academic supervisor on the institution's letterhead (describing the project, the relationship to the candidate and future collaboration), plus the supervisor's short CV, maximum 2 pages.
Short CV (maximum 2 pages) of the home-university supervisor.
Email addresses of two professors in your field; they upload recommendation letters through the application system.
Certificates and transcripts. Documents not in English, French, Italian or German need certified translations (India accepts self-certification).
Passport copy; dual citizens submit both passports.
Confirmation of admission to the doctoral school.
requirements.conditional_rule: PhD applicants applying through a graduate or doctoral school

requirements.text: Portfolio as a PDF with a link or QR code. Music: recordings in three different styles (composers send scores). Visual arts: three artworks with sketches showing creation dates and your name and country. Other fields (dance, acting, writing): recordings of performances or creations.
Confirmation from the Swiss university of the arts or music that you are admitted, or that admission is under review or pending.

application_steps.title: Check your country's offer and eligibility
application_steps.detail: Look up your country in the official A-Z list to see which scholarship types are offered, when the call opens, the country deadline (11:59 PM Swiss local time) and the Swiss embassy that is your contact. Then check eligibility. Applying is free; the commission warns about fake offers that ask for money.

application_steps.title: Find a Swiss supervisor or admission
application_steps.detail: Research and PhD applicants must find an academic supervisor in Switzerland themselves, who writes a support letter; allow weeks or months. When you contact a professor, send a short CV, motivation letter, 2 to 3 recommendation letters and a 2 to 3 page research plan. Art applicants need admission, or proof of application, from a Swiss university of the arts or music.

application_steps.title: Register in the GO ESKAS application system
application_steps.detail: Create a SWITCH edu-ID with two-factor authentication (authenticator app or passkey), then start a new application in GO ESKAS with it and fill in the five-page form. Registration and application are free. Applications are not accepted by email or on paper. The 2027-2028 call opened on 20 August 2026 for most countries; other countries open between 28 August and 15 September 2026 in the list.

application_steps.title: Upload documents and submit before your country deadline
application_steps.detail: Upload the full document set for your scholarship type and name two professors as recommenders. Submit before your country's deadline, which in the 26 October 2026 list runs from early October to 30 November 2026 depending on the country. You may submit only one application at a time; you may apply at most three times for the same scholarship type.

application_steps.title: Commission assesses the applications
application_steps.detail: The Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students decides. For research and PhD it looks at the academic profile, research competence and motivation; originality and methodological quality of the project; and quality of supervision and potential for future collaboration. For art it looks at the artistic profile, qualifications and motivation, the portfolio, and enrolment availability at the chosen university.

application_steps.title: Decisions announced by the end of May
application_steps.detail: Award decisions for the following academic year are announced by the end of May at the latest. The official pages do not describe an interview stage.

application_steps.title: Start in Switzerland on 1 September 2027
application_steps.detail: All scholarships start on 1 September 2027. Holders must live in the city or canton of the host institution, follow the commission's instructions, immigration law and institution rules, and report any additional income. Research fellows may not do fieldwork outside Switzerland.

application_steps.title: Renewal, supervision and return flight
application_steps.detail: PhD scholarships can be renewed twice up to 36 months if the first 12 months show academic progress; art scholarships can be extended to 21 months. The supervisor supports the holder during the whole research period. Non-EU/EFTA holders can use the flight allowance only for the return trip, within two months after the scholarship ends.

fetch_problems: The two PDFs (A-Z country list and GO ESKAS user guide) came back as binary; they were saved and read as text locally. The A-Z list's table layout is jumbled in text extraction, so only the date range and structure were read reliably, not a per-country mapping.
The regional PDF lists (Africa, Asia, Europe etc.) were not opened separately.
notes: The A-Z list read is the version of 26 Oct 2026; the stored nationality list came from the 1 Sep 2026 version, so the country list should be re-checked against the newer file.
The overview page says a maximum age of 35, while the at-a-glance page says born after 31 December 1991. Both are kept.

The overview page says applicants apply at Swiss diplomatic representations; the at-a-glance page says to use the online GO ESKAS system and no email or paper. The A-Z list names a Swiss embassy as contact per country.

The 26 Oct 2026 A-Z list shows the stored single deadline milestone 'depends on your country' is right: country deadlines run from early October to 30 November 2026, so many may already have passed on 13 Nov 2026.
Stored FAQ-derived fact kept: postdoctoral awards end from 2027/28 (stated in the FAQ, answer 13).
